title: Dedicated autoscaler: burst controls, throughput guarantees, and utilization reporting enhancement
author: Maya Liu
description: Motivation: dedicated fleets have observed burst storms and noisy utilization metrics under mixed-priority workloads. This PR introduces refined burst-token controls, conservative throughput guarantees, and richer utilization reporting to make autoscaling behavior more predictable for Dedicated customers. Summary of changes: 1) Implement token-bucket smoothing on burst windows to avoid instant fleet-wide scaling events; 2) Add per-priority throughput guarantees and admission control hooks so high-tier customers retain baseline throughput during contention; 3) Emit detailed utilization metrics (per-fleet, per-priority, per-epoch) and new labels to tie utilization to rollout and model version; 4) Add an offline compatibility migration tool for legacy token config; 5) Update docs and console dashboards; 6) Add unit and integration tests and CI gating. Testing and rollout: locally validated with perf-canary harness (steady-state and burst replay), staged canary on production fleet with 10% traffic, monitored via new dashboards for 48 hours. Rollout plan includes a 24h canary, gradual ramp to 50%, and an automatic rollback if median tail latency or error rate exceed configured SLOs. Checklist: - [x] Design doc linked - ENG-4321 - [x] Unit tests - [x] Integration tests in perf-canary - [x] Docs/console update - [x] Backwards compatibility migration tool - [x] Observability dashboards updated Notes: this is backwards-compatible by default; new throughput guarantees require an opt-in config per-customer. See release notes for admin flags.
